The control for drift detection on a workspace, the engine watching it for changes made outside Turf between convergences: enabled turns detection on or off; settle, sweep and confirm change how it watches. Name at least one; the rest stand. Turning detection on or off is the user's choice either way: call this only on their words, never on your own. The sweep reads every managed object unattended against the provider's API with the engine's credentials. enabled: false stands alone, and turns detection off even before the workspace has state (it overrides an up's drift: { … } still running). Detection needs the sweep to signal a change, and a standing seal (taken from a converged round) for confirm: turn it on with a sweep. Returns the settings as they now stand, and outcome: configured (detection is on with these settings; next: the watch), stored (the settings are kept, but detection is off: the note gives the call that turns it on), or disabled (detection is off; any open notices were closed).

**[Tiers](/docs/reference/server/#tiers):** full

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_alias` | string | no | Workspace alias, as 'open' named it. Omit for the workspace opened without an alias ('default'). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | true turns drift detection on (with any settings named in the same call); false turns it off, closing its open notices, and stands alone: the settings stand while it is off. Only on the user's words. |
| `settle` | integer | no | Seconds a changed object must be quiet before its signal is confirmed and becomes a notice; 0 takes the engine's default (30). |
| `sweep` | integer | no | Seconds one sweep cycle takes to read every managed object, unattended, against the provider's API with the engine's credentials; 0 turns the sweep off. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | false: no confirming read, so every notice stays unconfirmed and the sweep, which is that read on a cycle, does not run; true: confirm reads a settled object against the standing seal (the default). |
